claims.text: The driver's own trace shows the longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run was 143 seconds, which is 37 seconds short of the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present.

The trace is IMPAIRED (issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE, weight_multiplier 0.39): a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 sits inside the waiting window, and coverage is only 73.4%. I disclose this. The shortfall finding survives the discount because the gap can only make the measured dwell an UNDERCOUNT of the true dwell, and even the most generous reading of the record — the accumulated_dwell figure of 203 seconds — is still below the 180-second minimum only if the gap is treated as continuous presence, which the trace cannot certify. The 143-second longest run is the figure the policy directs the Judge to use (shortfall_basis = longest_run_sec).

The driver's arrival marker is not a GPS_AUTO platform event — trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON — so POL-NS-12 does not rescue the arrival or the waiting clock, and the dwell must be measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix under POL-NS-02, which is what the derived arrival block does.

The driver cannot accumulate dwell across the two separate in-geofence intervals to reach the minimum, because POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covering the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no advisory covers Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres in this window — so limb (i) is unavailable and the two runs (60 s and 143 s) cannot be summed.

The rider filed this dispute and the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the $4.50 cancellation fee is presently being carried by the rider. A full refund of that fee is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

The rider's own conduct is not the issue and I do not need it to be: POL-NS-06 is strict liability on the waiting period — a rider who was genuinely absent still gets the fee back if the driver cancelled before the minimum elapsed. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so no rider message can be shown, but that is irrelevant to this clause.

I concede that the rider's track is absent from the trace (rider_presence.available false, rider_fix_count 0), so POL-NS-04 limb (c) cannot be run and POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Under POL-NS-11 that test is UNDECIDABLE and neutral, and the fee is decided on the driver's own evidence — which is what POL-NS-06 does here.

The driver's counterparty statement — 'I waited the full time' — is contradicted by his own trace, which shows a longest continuous in-geofence run of 143 seconds against a 180-second minimum. The record, not the assertion, decides.

claims.text: The trip record shows a driver 'arrived' event at 11:32:47 and the trip terminated by the driver at 11:39:28 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises. Limbs (a) and (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show are therefore satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The driver's in-geofence dwell is measured by the derived arrival block as a longest qualifying run of 400 seconds, from 11:32:47 to 11:39:27, against a STANDARD-zone minimum dwell of 180 seconds. That is 220 seconds more than the free waiting period in force, so POL-NS-01(c) is satisfied with room to spare. I disclose that this derived figure comes from EV-GPS-02756, which the pre-pass tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE; the claim survives the discount because the run is bounded by the platform's own arrival and cancellation timestamps in the unimpaired trip record, and because the gap sits inside the run rather than at its edges.

The arrival marker is not a false one. The trip record carries arrival_marker BUTTON, and the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix under the derived arrival block is at 11:32:47, the same second as the recorded 'arrived' event, with a dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0. There is no distance-over-300m or speed-at-or-above-15kph mismatch between the marker and the trace, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock and the clock runs from the marker as recorded.

The rider's own track is absent from the trace: derived.rider_presence reports available false with rider_fix_count 0. Under POL-NS-11 that absence is UNDECIDABLE rather than adverse, it does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence, and it does not engage POL-NS-09(e). The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04 on a test that could not be run, and the fee is decided on the driver's evidence.

The chat log is empty: zero messages, first_message_at and last_message_at both null, and the trip record's chat_message_count is 0. There is therefore no rider message during the waiting window that could trigger POL-NS-04(a), and no rider statement of a correct entrance, block or tower that could strip the driver's compensation under POL-NS-03(i). The rider's claim that he 'was there' is unsupported by any contemporaneous message.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation_fee line is 4.50, total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The 4.50 matches the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd in force for this trip, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the amount the driver's compensation is computed on is sound.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is below the threshold of 4, and 0 divided by completed_trips_30d of 85 is 0.0, which is not greater than 0.08. Both limbs must hold and neither does, so compensation is payable rather than withheld. I note that driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 2, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-NS-07 expressly forbids substituting it for the trailing-30-day figure.

Compensation follows at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force: 80 percent of SGD 4.50 is SGD 3.60, which is the driver_compensation figure the fare breakdown's own derived money block computes under POL-NS-07. The residual 20 percent is the platform service fee. The driver drove to the pickup, held position for the full waiting period and cancelled only after the rider failed to appear, and the ruling should say so in cash.

The rider's filing history does not open an escalation route. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the 3-or-more threshold in POL-NS-09(d), and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so the 2-or-more same-pair test in POL-NS-09(c) is not met. Nothing in the record requires this case to go to a human reviewer.

I concede one point against my side. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. The derived arrival block shows two runs, 60 seconds and 143 seconds, separated by a 197-second gap, and the accumulated dwell of 203 seconds would fall short of the 180-second minimum only if the runs could not be summed. I do not rely on limb (i) and do not assert it against a MISSING artifact; the driver's case rests on the single continuous 400-second qualifying run, which needs no accumulation.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the deciding question in this case cannot be answered on the record as it stands, so I issue no money ruling. The $4.50 cancellation fee is held — not refunded to the rider and not released to the driver — while a human reviewer settles it.

What the record does establish. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02756, weight 1.00) shows the driver pressed 'arrived' at 11:32:47 and terminated the trip at 11:39:28 as RIDER_NO_SHOW, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met on the reason code. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02756, weight 1.00) charges $4.50, which equals the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd in force, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the figure in dispute is sound. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02756, weight 1.00) is empty: the rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04(a) (no locating or coordinating message), and no rider statement of an entrance or block strips compensation under POL-NS-03(i). POL-NS-03 does not otherwise apply — the driver's qualifying fixes are inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, not outside it — and POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill of $2.25 is not available because registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more.

Why limb (c) cannot be decided. POL-NS-01(c) needs a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period. The only artifact that speaks to the driver's in-geofence position is EV-GPS-02756, and it is impaired: it carries a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 sitting inside the waiting window (policy-level impairment under POL-NS-08(b), which fires above 120 seconds), and the pre-pass tags it GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE at weight 0.39. The trace shows two separate qualifying in-geofence runs, 60 seconds and 143 seconds, and it cannot show what happened between them. POL-NS-06(i) would let the runs be added (60 + 143 = 203 seconds), but that route requires a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING at weight 0.00, so the runs cannot be summed. The driver's 'I waited the full time' statement carries no weight and fills nothing. Limb (c) is therefore undecided over the unobserved stretch, and an undecided limb supports neither the fee nor a refund of it.

The drivers' arguments. (1) Limbs (a) and (d) satisfied — accepted, but the fee needs all four limbs and limb (c) is undecided. (2) 'Dwell 400 seconds' — not accepted. The 400-second figure is the span that bridges the unobserved gap (60 + 197 + 143 = 400), not a measured continuous dwell; the trace cannot certify presence across the gap, and the derived block's own shortfall basis is the 143-second run. (3) Chat empty, no rider message — accepted; it defeats POL-NS-04 and POL-NS-03(i), but it decides fault allocation, not the dwell. (4) Fare ledger reconciles — accepted; no fare defect. (5) Anti-farming does not trip — accepted: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 and 0 / 85 completed trips is 0.0, so neither limb of the POL-NS-07 test holds, and I do not use prior_no_show_flags, which POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-01 forbid for that test. (6) Compensation of $3.60 (80% of $4.50) — not reached: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, so no compensation issues. (7) No escalation route via the rider's or driver's dispute counters — accepted: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire; escalation arises under POL-NS-09(a) and (e) instead.

The rider's arguments. (1) 'Longest continuous run 143 seconds, 37 seconds short of 180, so refund in full' — the 143-second run is indeed the longest measured continuous dwell and it does fall short, but the 197 unobserved seconds could conceal continued presence, so limb (c) is undecided rather than failed and cannot carry a refund. (2) The $4.50 is charged and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — accepted as the state of the money; the fee is held rather than refunded. (3) POL-NS-06 is strict liability and the empty chat is irrelevant — accepted that the empty chat does not decide the dwell, but the clause still needs a measured dwell shorter than the minimum, and no such measurement can be certified here.

Why this escalates, and what the reviewer must settle. The deciding fact — whether the driver's in-geofence dwell reached 180 seconds — rests on a single artifact, EV-GPS-02756, at weight 0.39, which is below the platform confidence floor of 0.70 carried in this policy file (POL-GEN-02(2), POL-NS-09(a)); and that same artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) as the sole evidence for the deciding fact (POL-NS-09(e)). Escalation is terminal: no money moves and the $4.50 stays frozen. Open question for the reviewer: on the raw or full-resolution trace, did the driver remain inside the 50 m pickup radius continuously from 11:32:47 to 11:39:28, or did he leave and re-enter during 11:33:47–11:37:04? If he held position throughout, the fee stands at $4.50 and the driver's payout is $3.60; if the continuous dwell was under 180 seconds, POL-NS-06 refunds the $4.50 in full. If the reviewer needs more, the missing item is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02756-01. For routing: any monetary figure here ($4.50) would sit below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, but nothing executes while the fee is held.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your $4.50 cancellation fee is not being refunded now. To the driver: you are not being paid now. Both questions turn on one fact this record cannot settle - whether the driver held position inside the 50 m pickup geofence at Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres for the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip - so the fee is held and a human reviewer decides. What the record does establish: the trip record (weight 1.0) shows the driver's 'arrived' marker at 11:32:47 and the trip terminated by the driver at 11:39:28 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 are made out. The fare ledger reconciles: $4.50 charged, $0.00 refunded, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and $4.50 is the correct figure if the fee stands. The chat log holds no messages, so no rider message can trigger POL-NS-04(a) and no rider statement of an entrance, block or tower can strip compensation under POL-NS-03(i); the rider's assertion that he was there has no contemporaneous support in this record. What is not established, and why the case cannot be decided here: the only artifact measuring the dwell is EV-GPS-02756, and it is impaired - coverage 73.4% and a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 inside the waiting window, issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE, weight_multiplier 0.39. Its two measured in-geofence intervals are 60 s (11:32:47-11:33:47) and 143 s (11:37:04-11:39:27). The 400-second figure the driver relies on is the span from first fix to last fix and it swallows the unobserved gap; POL-NS-06(i) will not let the two intervals be added (60 + 143 = 203 s) because the traffic advisory it requires, EV-ADVIS-02756-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0). So the driver's limb (c) claim fails on the 400-second figure - continuity across the gap cannot be certified - and the derived block's own shortfall basis is the longest measured run, 143 s, 37 s short of the 180 s minimum. But the rider's shorter-run claim does not decide it the other way either: 143 s is a lower bound, and the same unobserved stretch could have kept the driver in place for the full 400 seconds. Limb (c) is undecided over the stretch the defect covers, and an undecided limb supports neither a fee that needs it nor a refund that needs it to fail. Considered and not decisive: POL-NS-11 applies to the absent rider track (rider_fix_count 0) - that absence is neutral, does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence and does not by itself escalate. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 0 and 0 / 85 = 0.0, below 4 and 0.08), so had the no-show been verified the driver's compensation would have been $3.60, 80% of $4.50; it is not payable on an unverified record. No referral is produced: POL-NS-05 does not fire (the first qualifying in-geofence fix falls at the arrival-marker second, so there is no false-arrival record to enter) and POL-NS-07's packet instruction applies only where the anti-farming check trips. Why this is an escalation: under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped by the artifacts that carry the deciding fact. The dwell is carried by EV-GPS-02756 alone; no independent artifact carries it, because the trip record's wait time is not an independent measurement (POL-NS-12 covers only a platform GPS_AUTO arrival, and this trip was marked by button). The cap is therefore 0.39, below the 0.70 confidence floor, and the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b). The ruling is ESCALATE under POL-NS-09(a) and POL-NS-09(e), read with POL-NS-08's closing sentence. No money moves: the $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. The open question for the reviewer, who is asked to settle it: did the driver remain continuously inside the 50 m geofence between 11:33:47 and 11:37:04, so that the effective dwell reached 180 seconds? A full-resolution GPS export of that window from the platform's own stream is the record-type evidence that would answer it (POL-GEN-04(b), POL-GEN-06(4)).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the disputed $4.50 no-show fee is placed on hold. No refund issues to the rider and no compensation is paid to the driver by the automated pipeline; a human reviewer will decide the case (POL-NS-09, POL-GEN-03). My confidence is capped at 0.39, below the 0.70 floor, so escalation is mandatory.

What is settled. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02756, weight 1.00) carries an 'arrived' marker at 11:32:47 and a driver termination at 11:39:28 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and the reason code in limb (d) are met. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02756, weight 1.00) reconciles: cancellation_fee $4.50 equals total_charged $4.50 and matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50; payment_status is CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd $0.00, so the rider presently carries the charge. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

What the case turns on, and why it cannot be decided. The fee stands or falls on POL-NS-01(c) read with POL-NS-06: a CONTINUOUS in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period in force. The only artifact that measures that dwell is the GPS trace EV-GPS-02756, and it is impaired at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE. It carries a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 — inside the waiting window, and longer than the 120 seconds POL-NS-08(b) makes a policy-level impairment — over 73.4% coverage. Over exactly that 197-second stretch the trace is silent, and that stretch is decisive: the driver's admitted in-geofence fixes are 7 fixes over 60 seconds (11:32:47–11:33:47) and 15 fixes over 143 seconds (11:37:04–11:39:27), 203 seconds in all.

The driver's case (the 400-second run) fails on that impairment. The 400-second figure is the span from the first to the last qualifying fix and it runs straight through the 197-second silence, so it does not certify continuous presence; and the two shorter runs cannot be added together, because the only provision that permits summing separate in-geofence intervals, POL-NS-06(i), requires a traffic advisory that is present and populated, and no advisory covers this pickup point (EV-ADVIS-02756-01, MISSING, weight 0.00).

The rider's case (the 37-second shortfall) fails on the same impairment. The trace's own gap-aware computation takes the longest continuous run, 143 seconds, and finds a 37-second shortfall against 180 seconds; but that finding, in either direction, rests on the same impaired trace over the same unobserved stretch. Whether the driver remained inside the 50 m arrival radius between 11:33:47 and 11:37:04 is precisely what the impaired trace cannot show, so the dwell limb is undecided over that stretch and supports neither the driver's payment nor the rider's refund.

Consequence: the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b), so under POL-NS-08 the ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND and the case escalates under POL-NS-09; POL-NS-09(e) so provides, and POL-NS-09(a) is independently met because a fact carried only by an artifact at weight 0.39 cannot be relied on above the 0.70 floor. Escalation is terminal: the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded.

Points answered. The driver's anti-farming point is right on its own terms — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 (and 0/85 = 0.0), so the POL-NS-07 check does not trip and compensation is not withheld on that ground — but no compensation issues on this ruling while the dwell is undecided; the mention of prior_no_show_flags is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and is properly disclaimed and not used. The driver is also right that POL-NS-09(c) (same-pair disputes both 0) and POL-NS-09(d) (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0) do not fire; (a) and (e) do. The empty chat log (EV-CHAT-02756, 0 messages) means POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider and POL-NS-03(i) cannot strip compensation — no rider message exists either way — and POL-NS-06's strict-liability reading is correct in principle, but a shortfall still needs a measurement this record cannot supply. No referral is produced: POL-NS-05 does not fire (the arrival marker coincides with the first in-geofence fix, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0) and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch does not trip.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the driver's device stayed inside the 50 m arrival radius throughout 11:33:47–11:37:04. If it did, the continuous dwell was about 400 seconds, POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, the $4.50 fee stands and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80% of $4.50 = $3.60. If it did not, summing the 60-second and 143-second runs is barred (no advisory), the effective dwell is 143 seconds, and POL-NS-06 refunds the whole $4.50 with no driver compensation. The full-resolution GPS stream covering the 197-second gap is the record that would settle it.

To the rider: your $4.50 is neither collected nor refunded today. To the driver: your payout is neither paid nor refused today. The case goes to a human reviewer and the $4.50 stays held meanwhile.

What is not in dispute. The trip record EV-TRIP-02756 (weight 1.0, complete) shows the driver's 'arrived' event at 11:32:47 and the trip ended by the driver at 11:39:28 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limbs (a) and (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show are met. The fare ledger EV-FARE-02756 (weight 1.0, complete) reconciles to the $4.50 cancellation fee in force for this STANDARD-zone trip, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and no dispute about the amount: $4.50 is what the rider carries, and 80 percent of it — $3.60 — is the driver compensation the fare breakdown itself computes under POL-NS-07, the residual 20 percent being the platform fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against completed_trips_30d of 85, both limbs of POL-NS-07 being far below their thresholds, and prior_no_show_flags (2) is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 makes context only and POL-NS-07 expressly forbids substituting. Neither profile shows the same-pair pattern POL-NS-09(c) reads (no_show_disputes_30d 0, disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both sides). POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the arrival marker (BUTTON) is matched by the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix at the same second (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), and nothing puts the driver over 300 m out or moving at 15 km/h or more, so the marker is not shown to be false. The chat log EV-CHAT-02756 is empty (0 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count 0), so no rider message triggers POL-NS-04(a) and no rider statement of an entrance or block exists to strip compensation under POL-NS-03(i); and the rider's track is absent, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is undecidable and neutral under POL-NS-11 and cannot exonerate the rider.

The one fact that decides this case is how long the driver actually held position inside the 50 m pickup geofence. The only artifact that can measure it is the GPS trace EV-GPS-02756, and it is impaired under POL-NS-08(b): a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 sits inside the waiting window, and coverage is 73.4% (issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE; weight_multiplier 0.39). Both advocates disclosed the impairment, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, and the finding does not escape the discount: the gap is exactly where the deciding reading would have to be.

On the trace's own readings the driver's in-geofence fixes fall in two separate runs — 60 seconds from 11:32:47 and 143 seconds from 11:37:04 — giving a longest uninterrupted run of 143 seconds, 37 seconds short of the 180-second free waiting period in force (POL-NS-06); the derived block also reports a single 400-second 'longest qualifying run' stepping from the first to the last in-geofence fix straight over the hole. The two figures differ only in how that 197-second hole is read. Reading it as presence infers the driver never left; reading it as absence infers he did. The trace's own excursion analysis says only that the observed maximum is a lower bound and does not certify the leash, so it cannot certify either inference, and POL-NS-06(i) — the one route that would let the two runs be summed — is unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), the advisory having to be present and populated. Nothing else bridges the gap: the arrival marker is the driver's own button-press and POL-NS-12 does not apply to a BUTTON marker; the chat log is empty, so no message from inside the window fills it; and the driver's later statement 'I waited the full time' is not a contemporaneous record and does not satisfy the test POL-NS-01(c) sets for itself.

So the rider's POL-NS-06 claim (a 37-second shortfall, full refund of $4.50) and the driver's POL-NS-01(c)/POL-NS-07 claim (a 400-second dwell, fee stands, $3.60 compensation) rest on the same impaired trace and on nothing else. POL-NS-08 provides that a claim resting on an artifact impaired under limbs (a) to (d) cannot alone support a ruling against the party it disfavours, and that where the only evidence for the deciding fact is impaired the ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND and the case escalates. Both limbs of that sentence are met: neither reading can be preferred, and the ceiling would in any event have been a split rather than a whole allocation.

The ruling. I escalate under POL-NS-09(e): the sole evidence for the deciding fact — the in-geofence dwell — is impaired under POL-NS-08(b). In the alternative POL-NS-09(a) is engaged, my confidence being capped at 0.39 by the weight of that sole carrier, below the platform's 0.70 floor. Escalation is terminal: no refund and no compensation issue today, and the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded. (Both figures in play, $4.50 and $3.60, are below POL-GEN-05's $8.00 execution threshold, but nothing is executed under an escalation.) No referral fires: POL-NS-05(ii) is not engaged because the marker is not false, POL-NS-03(ii) is not engaged because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius and this is not a wrong-entrance case, and POL-NS-07's anti-farming branch does not trip. The open question for the reviewer, and the only one: did the driver remain inside the 50 m pickup geofence throughout 11:33:47 to 11:37:04? If yes, the effective dwell is 400 seconds, POL-NS-01 is satisfied, the $4.50 fee stands and the driver is paid $3.60 under POL-NS-07. If no, the effective dwell is 143 seconds, POL-NS-06 gives a 37-second shortfall, and the $4.50 is refunded in full with no driver compensation. A full-resolution GPS export covering the gap, or anything showing movement during it, settles the case either way.

ledger.claim: The trip record shows a driver 'arrived' event at 11:32:47 and the trip terminated by the driver at 11:39:28 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises. Limbs (a) and (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show are therefore satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The driver's in-geofence dwell is measured by the derived arrival block as a longest qualifying run of 400 seconds, from 11:32:47 to 11:39:27, against a STANDARD-zone minimum dwell of 180 seconds. That is 220 seconds more than the free waiting period in force, so POL-NS-01(c) is satisfied with room to spare. I disclose that this derived figure comes from EV-GPS-02756, which the pre-pass tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE; the claim survives the discount because the run is bounded by the platform's own arrival and cancellation timestamps in the unimpaired trip record, and because the gap sits inside the run rather than at its edges.

The arrival marker is not a false one. The trip record carries arrival_marker BUTTON, and the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix under the derived arrival block is at 11:32:47, the same second as the recorded 'arrived' event, with a dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0. There is no distance-over-300m or speed-at-or-above-15kph mismatch between the marker and the trace, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock and the clock runs from the marker as recorded.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-02756 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The rider's own track is absent from the trace: derived.rider_presence reports available false with rider_fix_count 0. Under POL-NS-11 that absence is UNDECIDABLE rather than adverse, it does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence, and it does not engage POL-NS-09(e). The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04 on a test that could not be run, and the fee is decided on the driver's evidence.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-02756 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The chat log is empty: zero messages, first_message_at and last_message_at both null, and the trip record's chat_message_count is 0. There is therefore no rider message during the waiting window that could trigger POL-NS-04(a), and no rider statement of a correct entrance, block or tower that could strip the driver's compensation under POL-NS-03(i). The rider's claim that he 'was there' is unsupported by any contemporaneous message.

The fare ledger reconciles: the cancellation_fee line is 4.50, total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The 4.50 matches the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd in force for this trip, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the amount the driver's compensation is computed on is sound.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is below the threshold of 4, and 0 divided by completed_trips_30d of 85 is 0.0, which is not greater than 0.08. Both limbs must hold and neither does, so compensation is payable rather than withheld. I note that driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 2, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-NS-07 expressly forbids substituting it for the trailing-30-day figure.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_no_show_flags

ledger.claim: Compensation follows at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force: 80 percent of SGD 4.50 is SGD 3.60, which is the driver_compensation figure the fare breakdown's own derived money block computes under POL-NS-07. The residual 20 percent is the platform service fee. The driver drove to the pickup, held position for the full waiting period and cancelled only after the rider failed to appear, and the ruling should say so in cash.

The rider's filing history does not open an escalation route. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, below the 3-or-more threshold in POL-NS-09(d), and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so the 2-or-more same-pair test in POL-NS-09(c) is not met. Nothing in the record requires this case to go to a human reviewer.

I concede one point against my side. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. The derived arrival block shows two runs, 60 seconds and 143 seconds, separated by a 197-second gap, and the accumulated dwell of 203 seconds would fall short of the 180-second minimum only if the runs could not be summed. I do not rely on limb (i) and do not assert it against a MISSING artifact; the driver's case rests on the single continuous 400-second qualifying run, which needs no accumulation.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-02756-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT
